text: Got it — I've started work on the `src/plugin/timezone/index.js` bug (the `dayjs.tz()` handling of timestamp / JS Date / Day.js object inputs). A fix is being worked out and verified against the existing timezone/utc tests now.
Noted — bug #2 (`Convert format Z` in `src/plugin/timezone/index.js`) is now being worked on in parallel with bug #1. I'll report as soon as each fix is verified against the existing test suite.
Bug #3 (`src/locale/nl.js`, Dutch `Do` ordinal) is now being worked on in parallel with #1 and #2. I'll confirm each fix as soon as it's verified against the existing test suite.
Bug #4 (`src/plugin/weekYear/index.js`, `yearStart: 4` handling) is now being worked on in parallel with #1–#3. I'll report each fix as soon as it's verified.

Bug #3 is fixed. `src/locale/nl.js` had the wrong Dutch ordinal (`n => `${n}.``, German-style) and, more subtly, the ordinal string was not bracket-escaped, so the base formatter re-tokenized it (`1ste` → `10te`, `2de` → `23e`). It is now `ordinal: n => `[${n}${n === 1 || n === 8 || n >= 20 ? 'ste' : 'de'}]``, matching moment's `nl` locale (`1ste, 2de, 3de, …, 8ste, …, 20ste, 31ste`). Verified for every day of 2017–2021 plus composite formats; full suite still green (56 suites / 524 tests) and lint clean.

Bug #5 (`src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js`, locale-specific AM/PM parsing) is now being worked on in parallel with #1, #2 and #4. Bug #3 is already fixed. I'll report each remaining fix as it's verified.

Bug #1 is fixed. Root cause: `d.tz(input, timezone)` always ran the input through `fixOffset`, which treats its argument as a *wall-clock* time to be interpreted in the target zone. For a number / JS `Date` / Day.js object the value is already an absolute instant, so the zone offset was applied twice (`dayjs.tz(1401638400000, 'America/New_York')` gave `2014-06-01T16:00:00-04:00` instead of `2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00`). Fix: non-string inputs are now delegated to the existing, correct `dayjs(input).tz(timezone)` conversion path; string handling is untouched. Verified for timestamp, `Date` and Day.js inputs across several zones, and the full pre-existing suite still passes (56 suites / 524 tests); lint clean.

Bug #4 is fixed. Root cause: `weekYear()` only handled the "December date belonging to week 1 of the next year" direction (`weekOfYear === 1 && month === 11` → `year + 1`) and was missing the symmetric case — an early-January date that still belongs to the last week (52/53) of the previous year must return `year - 1`. With `yearStart: 4` locales (en-gb, fr, cs, sk, zh-cn, …) `2016-01-01/02/03` are week 53 of 2015, so `weekYear()` wrongly returned 2016. Added `if (month === 0 && weekOfYear >= 52) return year - 1`. Verified exhaustively against moment for every day 2000–2030 across yearStart:4 locales and all weekStart/yearStart combinations; the pre-existing weekYear/weekOfYear/advancedFormat/locale-keys suites (155 tests) still pass and lint is clean.
Bug #6 (`src/plugin/duration/index.js`, `Creating milliseconds`) is now being worked on in parallel with #2 and #5. #1, #3 and #4 are already fixed and verified. I'll report the rest as they land.

Bug #6 is fixed. Root cause: `unitToMS` in `src/plugin/duration/index.js` had no `milliseconds` key, but `prettyUnit('milliseconds'/'ms'/'millisecond')` returns `'milliseconds'`, so `dayjs.duration(100, 'milliseconds')` (and `.add(1, 'milliseconds')`) multiplied by `undefined` → `NaN` (`toISOString()` returned `P0D`). Added `milliseconds: 1` to the table. Verified the two-argument form now matches the one-argument form and moment for `toISOString`, `asMilliseconds`, `milliseconds`, `asSeconds`, `add`/`subtract` and the `ms` alias; full suite still green (56 suites / 524 tests), lint clean.

Bug #5 is fixed. Root cause: the `A`/`a` tokens in `src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js` hardcoded English (`/[AP]M/`, `/[ap]m/`, `input === 'PM'`), so any locale-specific meridiem (zh-cn 上午/下午, ja 午前/午後, ko 오전/오후, br a.m./g.m.) never matched and the parse produced an Invalid Date. Fix: `A`/`a` now use the generic word matcher plus a `meridiemMatch()` helper that scans hours 1–24 with `locale.meridiem(i, 0, isLowerCase)` and falls back to the English `PM`/`pm` comparison for locales without a `meridiem`. Verified AM and PM inputs for zh-cn/ja/ko/br against moment; full suite still green (56 suites / 524 tests), lint clean.

Status on bug #2 (`Convert format Z`): still in progress — the fix and its verification (against the existing timezone/utc suites under several TZ values) are being finished now. Bugs #1, #3, #4, #5 and #6 are fixed and verified.
